sections.teaching:
Concepts are extremely easy to understand, the PowerPoint includes all key points and it’s full of pictures. You just have to understand the concepts behind and remember a few things before exam. If you spend around 2-3 hours to go over it before mid-term, you can get an average, which is a B range. If you aim higher, do attend her lectures even it don’t take attendance (except negotiations and team presentations, you must attend those lectures to gain 3% attendance points, nothing special or any prepare needed, just appear then it’s fine). There are quite a lot of group activities in class, sometimes you would be randomly grouped and sometimes you would be grouped by your group project’s group. Her lectures are always interactive and she is opened to hear some different or funny answers. But two things to remember, do not talk with your mates in class and do not be late, she hates that…

Both midterm and final will include questions that directly related to what we actually did in the lecture, which the concepts behind may not be written in the ppt, you need to recognise by yourself. If you miss the class, it is encouraged to watch the lecture videos, then you will understand what’s going on in class, what have been discussed, this will help you a lot in exams.

I would say it’s not difficult to get A range compared to other 3 credits courses.

This course is very interesting. Unlike traditional management courses (e.g., MGMT 2010), it places greater emphasis on conceptual understanding and case analysis (i.e. empirical study) , instead of pure memorization. We can learn OB theories that are closely tied to daily life and can be applied everywhere in our everyday experiences.

What impressed me most is the concept of the moderator (contingency factor), which can sometimes significantly affect the correlation between independent and dependent variables. This has also inspired me that, when conducting management research in the future, we should not consider only a single factor. Beyond the research subject itself, the researchers also need to pay attention to various potential moderators, from the external environment and internal individual differences, that may influence the experimental results.
sections.teaching:
Carmen is definitely one of the BESTTT professors at UST. Although she has a Cantonese accent, we all got used to her delivery and pace after the first week.

Carmen is a very capable teacher. She can clearly and logically translate those hard-to-understand OB theories into straightforward, plain cases for us to grasp. At the same time, she places great emphasis on empirical study in class. After explaining each concept, Carmen always presents us with the research design and final results of relevant papers, usually shown in various charts and graphs. This gave us a preliminary understanding of research methods, showing us how to set up experiments and how to interpret experimental outcomes. Her teaching style goes beyond simply following the syllabus. Instead, she teaches us more about methodology.

Moreover, she is a kind and considerate professor. Since this course has about 10% participation (tbh, that’s quite a lot,,, it could determine the final grade...), she deliberately picks students who rarely raise their hands when asking questions and leading discussions, in order to accommodate those who are more introverted and hesitant to speak. Meanwhile, if she notices that you have been raising your hand the whole class but haven’t been called on, she will promise you that you are next. So, if you want to participate more, be sure to raise your hand firmly in class and give her a very confident look.

You get 6 points for the first card you get, but the points diminish with each additional card you get. So try to participate in class as much as possible (one participation card per class will definitely guarantee you get the whole points, but that's TOOOOOOOO exhausting). I got nine cards, so I guess I got the maximum points.

Exam 1: 27/30
Exam 1 covers Topics 1 through 5. NO CHEAT SHEET ALLOWED. It consists of 20 multiple‑choice questions and a 10‑point short‑answer question. The scope of the exam is not very large, so everyone performed quite well. The reading load for the MCQs is relatively heavy, so it is advisable to get as familiar as possible with the concepts. For the long‑answer section, there will be approximately one to two sub‑question that tests your ability to recite a concept from memory, but in practice you are not required to reproduce it word for word, just getting the general meaning right is sufficient.

Exam 2: 32/35
NO CHEAT SHEET ALLOWED. Exam 2 covers Topics 1 through 10. According to the announcement, the focus will be on Topics 6 to 10, and that was indeed the case. Only about 20% of the MCQs came from Topics 1–5. However, this does not mean you can completely skip reviewing Topics 1–5, because the short‑answer questions may unexpectedly include some earlier content. If you are not well prepared, you might lose some points (every single point MATTERS if you are aiming for an A range).

In addition, I think it is very important to review every single page of the slides, and especially not to overlook any details of the empirical studies, as they may appear in the exam in the form of a case or as an option in a MCQ. Of course, as I mentioned in the CONTENT section, this is not a memorization course. What you need to do is understand and apply. So, attending classes regularly and understanding the material as you go can significantly reduce the pressure of final revision.

Presentation: 82/100
Probably the lowest in class, because we didn't quite get the professor's instructions, which led us to make some silly mistakes. My suggestion is to listen to Carmen more, and if you are unsure about anything, send an email or privately schedule an office hour to ask for clarification.

Peer evaluation: ?/6 (Not announced)

Final grade: A+ (thx Carmen <3)
sections.workload: In summer term, the one-semester course condensed into two months can be somewhat exhausting. One class covers one topic, which means you gonna have an exam every month, and in the second month you also need to allocate time and energy to prepare for the presentation (the presentation and the final are in consecutive weeks). So there is a bit of pressure, but it's not a big deal, just do your best! Carmen will be kind to you as long as you put in the effort.

In-class exercises is group/individual exercises once per lesson (attendance), allowed to miss up to 3 exercises without penalty.

Class discussion is participation credits. The first participation would get 6/12 (half) of the overall participation score, and the upcoming participations with diminishing scores each (by a specific function that the student participated most would get full mark). So it is strongly encouraged to participate at least once.

Both exam are closed book. Exam 1 covers topic 1-5 and is 70 mins, exam 2 covers topic 1-10 (with emphasis placed on topics 6-10) and is 90 mins. There are ~20 MCQ and 2-3 long essay questions for each exam. The score allocation for MCQ:LQ is around 2:1. Sample questions are provided before exam.

Team project is a presentation during the last lessons, only ppt is required for submission, no reports needed. Only the slides are graded. 15 minutes presentation + 5 minutes of Q&A. Not all members are required to present.

I feel that the grading is quite lenient, as I got an exam below mean and another above mean, still getting B+. I had this similar situation in other business core courses and all of them are C-ranges. The participation policy is also very good as answering once can already get half participation marks. At last a total of 190 participation cards are given out for a 52-student class, and it is very competitive for participation each lesson :)

In class exercises: Group discussions and a worksheet for your group to complete. Can miss up to 4 without penalty.
Class discussion: Your average parti, answer questions during class. There will be plenty of chances for you to get parti. Near the end of the semester, Carmen will give priority to those who have never answered questions, so don't worry too much about it.

Exam 1: AI generated MC questions.
Exam 2: Short essay questions. Word limit on answers. Heavy on application. In my paper we had a chance to show what we learnt in the course that was not mentioned in other questions.
Both exams are application-based, but without sufficient memorisation on the various theories and theoretical solutions, you will do poorly.

Project: Read an academic paper assigned to your group by lucky draw. Interview someone. Come up with solutions and present in class. Reading from script is allowed, as long as you maintain eye contact with the audience. Some groups asked other ppl to ask them scripted questions so that they can prepare beforehand (we did not do that). All teams in my class put in a lot of effort so the competition was fierce.
Progress report: A one-page report for Carmen to understand your group's progress after midterm. Carmen will hold a consultation session with your group and explain what needs to be changed and answer any questions. Graded on effort.

Research participation: Participate in research experiments. Just show up and finish the experiments and you will get the credits.

Lecture recordings provided.
sections.workload:
The project can be painful if you have bad groupmates, as with any group projects. Thankfully, my groupmates are all high-achievers and it went smoothly for my group.

Read just like others, but Professor Ying's syllabus is actually nerfed from other sections, that i suspected the content is halved much more easier , while somehow adjusted to fit her research on gender diversity and crosscultural collaboration (which i found interesting)

unlike other sections, theres like no attendence for each lesson, with participation being group-based (the answerer get 2 points while everyone in the group gets 1 point); I think this is kinda ridiculous cuz sometimes people just yap about their personal experience on how it related to the organisational behavior topics, but I think this kind of win win system helps the team to engage more and have fun.

Usually in class, I'm 80% of the time doing random shit like scrolling for my other courses, doing other projects. That other 20% time is when Lin shows wacky stuff like Family Guy clips or gorilla dancing that my selective attention catches on.

Most people actually skip classes except the 5 required ones, and Lin's pretty chill about it.

I feel like if u really want to study Organisational behavior, Lin's content might not be too dense for you. But if your motivation to study MGMT is extrinsic and not intrinsic, then Lin's section is right for you!

Only thing i remember: final examination questions
Q1: Cialdini’s principle of influence
Q2: Negotiation types [distributive/integrative] & strategies - use 3 of them [BATNA, target, Anchoring, etc]
~ the case: u want to switch to another company, and ur boss now wants to negotiate with you for higher salaries / more flexible shifts to buy you back ~
Q3: tight culture vs loose culture [strict company culture case ]
Q4: one concept/theory you love so much
[ I answered situational leadership style ]

That's it; the exam is piss easy ; Don't ask why I remember because I have awesome memories.

eg :  "Scarcity : highlighting uniqueness / rarity of opportunity / idea / products ~ increasing likelihood of people pursuing them [ limited time offers / exclusive access ]. People tend to be afraid of regretting opportunities, thus prefer seizing the opportunity"

This is all I transcribed from Ling's speech, recited, and directly wrote all down in the exam, and that's enough !!!

My friend loves Lin's accent, so that's a plus (and she looks kinda pretty too)

sections.workload:
The main workload of this course primarily revolves around the group project. The group projects are typically organised into teams of 5-6 ppl. If your teammates are responsible enough and collaborate well, it shouldn't be too demanding (so it is very important to choose your groupmates carefully)

For the MT (Exam I), the questions are mostly MC. If you are good at memorisation, there's generally no need to worry. As long as you have a clear understanding of the concepts, you should be able to handle it.

For Exam II, the question format will be short-answer and short-essay questions (but with word limits). The exam is closed-book, so it relies more on your memory (it only tests your memory). Essentially, as long as you understand all the concepts clearly and memorise their definitions, you will get great marks. The only open-ended question is asking you to select a concept learned in this course and explain how it could help you in your future work.

For the Midterm, its literally just rote memorization and all mcqs. I remember one question was like asking what is the exact steps for implementing some concept and you need to remember the order of all 7 steps or something like that. You can just put all the concepts into anki flashcards and memorize it over the weekend and get a satisfactory grade so no complaints.

Final is much more flexible, its open ended questions and a lot of both the final and midterm has questions about things that happened DURING class so you have to attend all the classes or watch all the videos if you want full marks. The Final essay was nice, you're allowed to write your opinion on a particular situation and I think there's no real right answer you just need to apply what you learn't and back up your reasoning on the issue.

Presentation is pretty regular, its a presentation on a social issue and application of mgmt concepts on it. My team didn't do well but I remember there were a lot of creative presentations and I thought it was very funny, people brought construction helmets and everything to class to act.

sections.grading:
My Stats:
Exam 1 (20%): 45/60 (~80%)
Mean:74.496%, s.d. 13.286%, 84% or above = A range
All MC Question, not very hard but requires critical thinking

Exam 2 (28%): ?
3 Essay Writings, cheat sheet is allowed, the question is quite straightforward, btw in this year they don't really test content before midterm lmao.

I feel like I perform pretty well in this part, but I write too much and they don't provide extra papers, so yeah don't write too much like me lmao.

Research Participation (6%): 6/6
It requires you to do 3 questionnaires from the MGMT department, it takes around 1 hr to finish each of them, the grading is given by completion, so yeah a free 6% if you finish all of them on time.

Class Participation (16%): ?
Basically you just have to answer the question in class, and prof. CHAO will give you a blue card for credit. Prof. CHAO love to invite students to share their opinions, no matter the answer quality, she always gives the participation card. So if you attend enough classes and try to answer 1 question for each class, I guess you will be fine. For me, I think I get around 12-14 cards?

Btw for this course attendance is not counted, but if you wanna get  this 16% of participation, you should come to class regularly.

Team Project (Total 30%, split to two parts)
She provides four academic papers on different topics. Students are required to choose one of these papers and conduct their own analysis based on the topic. In each class, there are typically about 8 groups, and each paper is presented by two groups (first-come, first-served for topic selection). You can't choose your own group mates, the group list is assigned randomly.

Part 1: Final Report (15%): 8.7/10
12 pages maximum, double-line spacing, 12 font size new times roman, actually for a team with 7-8 people, you don't really need to spend that much of time on that, the grading I think is ok, our groups just finish it within 2 days lmao.

Part 2: Presentation (15%): 11.94/15
15 mins presentation about your own research findings, all group members have to present their own parts, 5-mins Q&A question session, students who ask Q&A questions can receive Participation Card.

I think the grading is ok, we didn't get a very high grade since we are a bit overrun, prof. CHAO did mentioned that there will be a slightly mark deduction for that. Try not to overrun if you can!

There's also 1 project kickoff meeting, which teaches you the secondary research skills, demonstrated by the librarian (?).

1 project progress report (but I don't think it counts on the project total mark, we get 95 for this).

And 2 peer evaluation, our groups we give good grades for each other so idk whether poor grading will affect others grade.
sections.workload:
One big problem is the randomly assigned grouping, if you get bad group mates, you will have a lot of trouble to finish all these things by yourself lmao.

Total workload is moderate, overall it's a pretty good course, I will recommend you to take her class, it's not that bad as what others said in the previous year.

Final Grade: B+

sections.content:
12 main Organizational Behavior (OB) topics. To be frank, I only remember 5 of them vividly, and only 2 of them are useful to my business journey. Needless to say, the topics aren't winning any practicality awards, but it could be engaging to some.

The OB topics are barely related to one another and are not cumulative. Within an OB topic, the sub-topics could be quite scatterred and sometimes too simple to be taught (aka common sense). Here's the list if you're interested.
1. Personality
2. Values and Perceptions
3. Attribution and Biases
4. Decision Making
5. Job Attitudes
6. Emotions
7. Motivation
8. Groups and Teams
9. Conflicts of Interest
10. Negotiation
11. Leadership
12. Power and Ethics
sections.teaching:
What's that? You don't like traditional teaching and learning? Well this professor is for you! Every lecture, you would feel like a kid engaging in class activities — sometimes even for the entire lesson so she barely even teaches!

In all seriousness, while her lessons have a lot of class activities (which I admit are pretty fun at times and makes me look forward to them), she barely teaches. She expects you to listen to her and not make any unnecessary noise or distractions (so no chitchatting, we're back in primary school yay). To put it into perspective, the professor would spend on average: 10 mins playing some online video (TED talk/ research video etc.); 20 mins teaching; 30 minutes conducting a class activity; 20 mins of free time to write your lesson reflection (meaning you may leave the lesson 20 mins early at times).

Her teaching style is to let you understand the OB topic through class activities. I respect it, honestly, and I do find it mostly enjoyable. However, after the activities, she does not explain the OB topic thoroughly enough. Also having disorganized PowerPoint slides do not help. More often than not, I, along with several others, are left puzzled during revision. This leads me to have mixed feelings for her teaching style.
sections.grading:
A.I. Grading.

It's already an issue if you use A.I. to grade our work, but please, at least state that you do so.

The fact that the guidelines are awfully vague with no concrete rubrics and mark allocation, along with low variation of marks across students, makes one question whether the one grading the work is my driving examiner, or simply a machine.

The grading issue is especially prominent during team project tasks. Progress Report marks were spread across 8.5-10/10, pretty amusing. Her comments demonstrated how "much" she read through our report, as she would suggest vague improvements we already wrote within the report.

The Presentation was much worse. The same low mark spread can be seen. However, what made me lose the little respect I had left, was from her behavior (ironic) during our presentation — constant yawns and extensive phone usage. What happened to ethics (ironic), good morals, and respect? She behaved this way for a selective number of groups, whilst paying full attention to a few others. Our A.I. speculations were further consolidated as her "comments" mentioned points for improvement that we already talked about during our presentation. Her "comments" had a hint of solely inputting our PowerPoint slide for A.I. to grade (also she still included syntax " * "), neglecting our presentation itself.

Finally, as for the Exam II (Final Exam), her requirement for the 3 essay question exam was "CLEAR and TIDY to read" handwritting. No concrete rubrics on what she wants from us, simply just sub-questions with mark allocations. And the word limit was not by word count, but instead by number of lines. Odd. Perhaps it's for A.I. to scan and read easier.

MGMT 2110 is an introductory course exploring individual and group behavior in contemporary organizations, blending theoretical and applied perspectives.

Key topics include:
Individual Level: Personality, values, attitudes, emotions, perception, learning, motivation, decision-making.

sections.grading:
Grading is way too overcomplicated.

Breakdown :
1. Knowledge-Based (40%)
Mid-Term Exam (20%): MCQ-based
Final Exam (20%): Essay-Based (Open-Book). Question is given before, but topics are very ambiguous and confusing
Formula: Score = 2 × √(Mid-Term Score × Final Exam Score).

2. Project-Based (35%)
Presentation (15%): 15-min group presentation
Written Report (20%): Wriiten version of group presentation.
Peer Evaluation: Adjusts individual scores (0-10 scale, divided by 10). Example: Group scores 13/15 (presentation) + 18/20 (report), peer evaluation 8/10 = (13 + 18) × 0.8 = 24.8/35.

3. Participation-Based (25%)
In-Class Exercises (10%): 5-7 submissions (satisfactory/unsatisfactory). Unsatisfactory work requires rework.
Attendance at Presentations (9%): Mandatory for all group presentations (Apr 22–May 6, 2025).
Research Participation (6%): 3 hours (three 1-hour sessions) in MGMT department experiments, announced later.

sections.workload:
The primary assessment for this course will be a group project. The project will involve the following components:

Introduction:

Briefly describe the real-world organizational behavior (OB) problem that your project addresses.
State the objectives of your project.
About the Interviewee/Organization:

Provide relevant background information about the person you interviewed and/or the organization involved, such as demographics, job duties, and nature of the business.
The Real-life OB Problem:

Describe the real-world OB problem in detail, including how the problem arises and the adverse impacts on employees and the organization.
Recommended Solutions:

Propose and justify your recommendations for addressing the OB problem.
Discuss the potential obstacles to implementing your recommendations and strategies for overcoming those obstacles.
Conclusion:

Summarize the key points presented in your oral presentation and written report.

The project will be assessed through both an oral presentation and a written report.

I genuinely loved this course, I loved the way he tied all the theory to anecdotes/real-life examples to we could get the point. Additionally, the course is designed in such a way that you always have your attention caught on what Dr. Wai is saying. It makes class more engaging. I think, however, that slides have just so much information in them, so that even sometimes one lecture is not enough to cover everything - I certainly want to note here that it is not Dr. Wai’s nor TA’s fault - perhaps the course itself is too broad. Dr. Wai definitely put so much effort simplifying all of the information, props to him and TA. Apart from knowledge, this course and especially Dr. Wai helped me grow more as a person. I felt as if I am stepping into another milestone, another chapter of my life. I don’t want to dramatic, but this course really had an impact to me more than just in terms of knowledge or business core - I really evolved after taking this course.

For participation, attend classes to fill out the handouts for discussion or raise your hands in class so prof recognizes your efforts.

For research, you need to attend three MGMT research questionaries I think one online and two you need to book and go into the computer barns.

For midterm and final, just revise based on the PPTs. Midterm is relatively harder because it's all MCs and they somehow seem quite off from the concepts on PPT. For a group project, you get a random group which for me was not very good. But you need to somehow show that you are working along with them as you need to show up in consultations, submit progress papers, and talk about work distribution in the final report. You need to submit a video (originally was a presentation, but prof changed it cuz no one was attending to see others present) and a final report. You are given the entire semester to do it, so don't put it till the last minute for this as it carries the most percentage of your grade.

sections.content:
Two main topics: individual behavior and team behavior.
Individual behavior is mostly covered in the midterm, final exam is non-cumulative and focuses more on the team.

Individual:
- Personality and Values
- Perception and Learning
- Emotions, Attitudes, and Stress
- Motivation
- Individual Decision-making (this topic is covered in the final)

Team:
- Team Dynamics
- Conflict Management
- Negotiation
- Leadership, Power, and Influence

Midterm: 50 MCQ; 50 points
Final: 6-7 short questions (each with sub-questions, usually a, b, c); 100 points
Class participation: answer or ask questions in class and receive a beige-colored slip of paper for participation credit.
Research: do 3 research experiments, each 20-40 minutes.
Group project: choose one topic from the list, then come up with your own research question, and prepare a 10-page report plus 15-minutes presentation

Topic list:
1) Authenticity in the workplace (e.g., authenticity on leadership, identity, networking etc.)
2) Business negotiation
3) Creative thinking and performance
4) Diversity (age, gender, race etc.) in the workplace
5) Effective decision making in workplace
6) Leadership in global organizations
7) Managing Organizational Change
8) The use of Artificial Intelligence in organizations

sections.workload:
Overall, I think the workload is relatively low.

- Participation/Attendance:
    - Attendance will not be taken during lectures but will be taken when it comes to presentations.
    - There will be some class assignment which is pretty easy; answering a few questions.

- Midterm Exam:
    - Midterm exam is closed-book
    - It consists of 60 MCs
    - Ellick says if our average score in the midterm exam is above 75%, then our final exam will not be cumulative.

- Final Exam:
    - Since our average score in the midterm exam is below 75%, our final exam is cumulative.
    - It is an open-book exam.
    - The final exam consists of 4 parts:
        - Part 1: 4 Short questions (questions that many of us get wrong in the midterm)
            - Ellick changes some details and the format of the questions.
            - You need to fully understand the logic behind when he gives the "future paper" during the lectures.
            - He may ask why you should do this action or what if the situation is... etc.. in the final exam.
        - Peer evaluation
            - Rate each of your groupmates on a scale of 0-10.
        - Part 1.5
            - We watch a video of Ellick explaining what is part 1.5 lol
            - There are 3 questions that free riders will not be able to answer (What is the independent variable/dependent variable/contingency factor mentioned in the assigned research paper?)
            - The number of questions you get correct determines the percentage of your score you get in part 2 (for example, if you get 1 question correct, then you will get 33.33% of the score you get in part 2)
        - Part 2: 3 Long questions
            - There are questions related to the problems encountered during the group project or solutions you would like to suggest.
            - There will be 4 areas, and each area contains 2 OB topics. You need to choose 2 areas.
            - You need to answer the questions according to the 2 areas chosen.

- Group Project:
    - Most workload of this course will be the group project.
    - Around 8-9 people per group. I think this number of people is quite a lot and according to what is taught in this course (more people in a group, less motivation to work because you expect others will work), you must expect there are some free-riders in your group.
    - I suggest attending the consultation session because Ellick explains what he expects us to do in the group project more thoroughly.
    - You are expected to define the iv (independent variable), dv (dependent variable) and contingency factor, give an introduction of the assigned research paper and come up with a solution (which is also the iv) based on the evidence suggested by the research paper. Remember all the things need to be supported by evidence from the research paper.

- Research:
    - There are 3 online research studies posted on Canvas. Each consists of 4 parts and takes around 1 hour to complete. Just answering some questions.
    - Remember to finish all to get full credit for the research participation.

sections.content:
Content is genuinely interesting and you can see yourself using what you were taught in this class in the future and in work. Simple things like team conflict and dynamics are taught in detail in this course, and it can really become useful when you start to actually work in the workplace and face issues in a team.

This is an introductory course to organizational behavior (OB) – the field of study that investigates how
individuals,  groups,  and  organizational  characteristics  affect  human  behaviors  and  organizational  
effectiveness.  

We live in an organizational world.  To succeed in your careers and to help your organizations succeed,
you have to understand how employees and managers behave and why they behave the way they do.  
This  course  will  help  by  covering  a  wide  variety  of  OB  topics  such  as  personality,  perception  and  
decision making, motivation, team dynamics, leadership, and power and influence.  While this course
will not turn you into OB experts right away, it should lay a good foundation to help you become more
effective and satisfied organizational members.

Both the midterm and final exams were open-book exams, if you revise using the presentation slides (which is what I did) it is more than enough to give you a clear overview and good understanding of the concepts and content in the course. Class participation was actually tracked (she has you write down in a discussion after each class what you said during each lecture) so make sure you make an effort to participate! The group project includes two reports and a presentation. The format of the report is given. The presentation would contain content from your final report but you would want it to be very creative, engaging and interesting for people to listen to if you want a higher score.
sections.workload: The workload isn't too heavy because the whole course is formatted in a progressive manner. There are a few assignments (some required, some optional) throughout the course for credit (they're super simple and short quizzes or writing tasks). Optional assignments give you extra credit. The group project really depends on your team (it's luck because it's assigned). Different friends of mine had varied approaches when it came to the project (most commonly they split a group of 6 into three teams of 2 to work on one OB issue), but my group all worked on every OB issue together based on the formatting for the report. If you work progressively throughout the semester, the workload is manageable.

sections.teaching:
Her teaching is excellent, you probably won't see a professor who is as good at teaching MGMT as her. I couldn't wait to have her lectures every time. She engages with the students very well by often asking open-ended questions and encouraging us to speak up since she really listens to us and there's no correct answer anyway. She's also very friendly and warm which makes it pleasant for us to hear her speak. The pace of teaching is appropriate (to me) so you won't feel like some parts are a waste of time.

MGMT is supposed to be boring in general but she plays a lot of relevant videos (especially real-life experiments) which are quite interesting and helps us understand the concepts very well ( some Qs in the MT are related to the videos too so better pay attention :) ).

She also occasionally sets up case exercises (I won't spoil them or it won't be fun for you) and in-class discussions for some topics which have case studies, which are quite entertaining and engaging too so I can almost guarantee you that you won't get bored from attending her lectures.

sections.content:
The content being caught in this course includes some basic concepts and introductory knowledge about management.

Course content:
- Organisational behaviour
- Personality and Values
- Emotions
- Perception and Decision Making
- Motivation
- Groups and Teams
- Communication
- Leadership
- Managing Globally

Personally I find the content in the Slides quite interesting and pretty easy-to-understand. As long as you read through the slides before the midterms and finals, I think you can still get a good grade without paying attention in class. But you do have to attend the class in order to get the full attendance.
sections.teaching: Carmen is a very nice professor!! She has a strong hk accent when she spoke in English but she explains the content clearly, and she welcomes her students to ask questions whenever they don't understand. She is always fun in class!! She tries to joke sometimes. There are also breakout room discussions (in random groups for each lesson) and each group has to submit a file on Canvas at the end of the class. We will sometimes watch videos together that makes the class less boring. Overall I like her teaching style!
sections.grading:
Components:
Class Participation 14%
Midterm Exam (MCQ) 20%
Final Exam (Short essay) 30%
Project (Presentation + Written Report) 30%
Research Participation 6%

For the participation part, try to answer more questions just like the other MGMT courses. (Though I did not answer any questions) Do remember to do the research surveys else you will lose points.

For the project part, my group worked hard but the other groups are much better, we got 2-3 points below mean:((( It is about a movie related to Organisational Behaviour. You just have to analyse the movie and then write about the related OB issues - not that hard to handle, but sadly we did not manage to score a better mark.

There is 1 midterm and 1 final exam, for the midterm all of them are Multiple Choice questions, that you have to understand the concepts clearly before the exam; but in the final they are all in the form of long questions, you have to type it out in a Word Document and submit it on Canvas. The grading is not that bad though, I got a B+.
sections.workload: I would say that the workload is fine, not that heavy compared to other business foundation courses. It will be a bit busy when you have to work on the project as you will have to prepare for both the presentation and the written report, but as long as you have good groupmates who won't freeride you, I think you will be perfectly fine. And you just have to revise on the midterm and final exam just a week or so before by going through the slides. Add oil guys!!

If you want to have good grade only, reg him! If you care more about what you will learn in the course, dun reg him.

Be active during lesson and going back for f2f lesson are the keys of getting good grade from this professor. (I tried to be more active and I went back for some f2f lessons as well). Only the first exam score released (around 0.8 sd above mean), other score were not disclosed and I got A finally.
sections.workload:
This course shouldn't be a heavy workload course but the professor increases quite a lot.

First, we need to prepare interesting findings and recap every lesson (group basis), but actually only spend you around 30 minutes outside the lesson for that.

Second, the group project is quite demanding but luckily we got 9 groupmates and we could evenly distributed the workload.

Third, in my opinion, exam has the heaviest workload. Since he didn't spend enough time on explaining concepts as well as not providing any lecture recording back (his PowerPoint slides are too simplify as well), I need to read the WHOLE textbook and search online myself, which uses a lot of time. This is the first course in ust that I have to read the whole textbook!

Carmen is a really nice, easygoing and passionate professor. :) She teaches wholeheartedly and she is friendly as well. She always tries to interact and chat with us. When we have questions, she is always happy to help us with detailed and clear explanation. The whole class loves her sooo much. :P

Overall, I think her teaching quality is pretty nice. She has a structured ppt with bullet points and it is good for revision. I'm also quite impressed that her time management for the lesson is quite well. She can always manage to finish everything on time.

Highly recommended!!!
sections.grading:
For me, grading is very nice. The midterm is all MC questions and final is short questions. Those questions are kind of straightforward. (Just some traps for the MC and you have to pay close attention to it)

For the participation marks, you have to get it by answering questions that Carmen has asked during the lesson, and doing some group assignments in breakout room. I am not sure how many marks does answering one question worth tho.

The project is not that difficult. It's mainly about presenting a movie using those concepts taught (stuff like that)

Also there is a part called research participation. Just attend it and you will get full marks for that.
(Basically everyone scored full marks)

Overall, the mean of the grading should be around B/ B+. A lot of my friends got A range in Carmen's class :D Good luck!!

Not much workload tbh. The main workload should be the project, just pray that you won't have free riders in your group (sadly my group has 1 so u know ...)

sections.workload: There are 2 exams, 1 progress report, 1 final report and 1 presentation in total. The exams are not very hard if you understand the concepts and know how to apply in daily life. Similar to the exams, the project examines the degree of your ability to apply OB concepts in your chosen movie while the presentation is testing your communication skills and team dynamics. Since the presentation will be spread out in 3-4 lessons, if you are arranged to present on the first day of the presentation, you might feel more pressured as it is the day of your final report deadline as well. And for the others, they might have more time to prepare for the power point and presentation. So, the workload depends.

sections.content:
Lots and lots of theories and research results... These are indeed something interesting to know, but it seems that the more important part for us is how real companies nowadays apply these managerial principles to handle different situations. It's such a pity that the content in this course remains in the ivory tower and does not really translate into something potentially useful in the real corporate world. Yep it does teach you the process of emotional regulation, but it does not help you increase your EQ. Yep it tells you where your leadership power comes from, but it does not help you become a good leader. Yep it teaches you the Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs and the Job Characteristic's Model, but after learning all these you still don't know how to motivate people.

I understand that OB principles should be evidence-based and well supported by research results, but I think we students want more than just research results. It's about how companies apply the principles, not just research results.

 What's OB?
 Personality and Values
 Emotion
 Perception and Decision Making
 Motivation
 Group & Teams
 Communication
 Leadership
 Managing Globally

sections.content: It is generally a really interesting course that explains how people think or behave in a work environment. It tries to build a connection between psychology and business, such that one knows how to better manage emotions within the company to maintain a good relationship. Some of them may be common sense, but some can be quite hard or even surprising to know. So learn this course with an open heart and don't dismiss it as something that you already know,

Week 1: introduction to organisational behaviour
Week 1-2: emotions and moods

sections.teaching:
Lucia is an extremely pretty and cheerful professor. She always gives out Kisses (chocolate) to us! She likes to ask questions in class so class is interactive. However, I feel like she reads from the powerpoint quite a lot of times.

I like that Lucia does not give out class participation mark by how much questions or answers you ask/answer in class. All class participation marks can be obtained by attending her game sessions and iPRS miniquizzes (super super easy). And, she even tells you when you can get these points in the timetable she released at the beginning of the course. But you have the responsibility to check the timetable as she won't remind you which classes have marks.

However, you will definitely have advantage if you answer questions in class, as Lucia will remember you and that will give you a HUGE advantage during group project and presentation.
sections.grading:

Final 30%, Essay
Team project 30%
Class participation 14%
Research participation 6%

although class content is easy, the midterm was quite tricky and grade statistics weren't that outstanding

final was on short questions (6 short essays, one page max) on respective topics

team project is on a movie analysis, where you have to analyse movie content and characters based on the OB concepts taught throughout the semester

class participation can be taken be attending class on time (iPRS before class every two lessons on a OB concept, really easy and you can discuss in class so almost everyone gets full marks)

research participation details will be sent via email, so don't worry about this as you will get all 6% by attending two management experiments/surveys organised by the department
sections.workload:
Workload is super light. The quizzes are so easy you can just read the powerpoint slides 5-10 minutes before class and still score full mark. The group project was tough for me as my group mates were all either free-riders (you can't choose your own group mates), or gave really low quality work. So I almost had to do the entire project on my own which was tough as I deadline-fought.

If you manage your time well, things should be quite easy to finish in a short amount of time as the OB concepts are easy to "blow-water" from the movie.

The project includes a mid-project short paper (2 pages, not graded), a group presentation and a final report (forgot how many pages, but much longer than mid-project paper)

sections.teaching:
Professor Tali is a very knowledgeable and generous person to start with. She is interactive and if you are an active student in the class, she will remember your name (which is important if you want a good grade in the end).
Although she may seem like a rookie in SBM, she was professional and as her student, it was comfortable to be in her classes. Anything you didn't know she would try her best to answer and explain.
I highly recommend registering for this instructor.
sections.grading:
Grading is rather lenient, which what all students like to hear.
Important components are mid-terms, finals, and the group project.
Mid-terms was MC, Finals was all short essay type questions; not difficult at all. As long as you are able to effectively show that you can process, explain and apply the teaching contents in the assignments, you will be fine.
For the group project, pray hard that you get good teammates because this can be the turning point for your grades for this course. This is not the kind of group project where you can manage it on your own. I was very lucky to have good teammates. You will be required to choose a movie and analyze it according to the concepts taught in class; again, not difficult as long as everyone plays their part.
P.S.: A+
sections.workload:
All you have to do is one midterm, one final exam, 2 participation documents, one group project (with a progress report, a final report, and a presentation) and participate in required research studies.
The workload is generally distributed very evenly and as a student, I found it easy to cope with what this course requires me to submit and deliver. The workload is very reasonable. For mid-terms and finals, if you study hard, it is easy to reach up to 80-90%.
Sometimes she uses iPRS to take attendance, but most importantly, participate actively.

sections.workload:
Simple and straightforward as long as u elab and connect everything tgt.

For midterm, it consists of 56 MCs. She will ask u basically everything including OB table, Hofstede's Cultural dimensions, Mintzberg's managerial roles. (some qs are just directly copied from the lecture ppts) so copy everything on lecture ppt will do.

For project, groupmates will be assigned according to an OCEAN personality test. My group consists of 4 types of people who are more relationship-oriented, focus on big picture, detail-minded (conscientious), and spontaneous people. It worked okay for us. You have to pick an OB movie and apply theories to explain the behaviours (whether it is effective/ineffective). Include as many concepts as possible and link everything tgt.

For project presentation, be as creative as possible. Although you are asked to wear smart casual, people do talk shows, drama, role plays etc (there is a creativity mark for presentation)

For final, just like the project, link everything tgt. there are 6 short questions. You are allowed to bring 1 A4 cheat sheet. just write every definition on it and link everything tgt. super easy

sections.teaching:
Her way of teaching makes the course thought provoking and fun. She encourages students to participate (but doesn't base final grade on class participation) by rewarding us with candies. She is so kind and warm and loving.

She gives very concrete real life examples while explaining about concepts and encourages team discussion so we can really grasp what she is talking about. Also, her PPT is very simple and easy to read with very little text, so reviewing for exams are not that hard. In addition, I feel like I already understand a lot just by listening in class.

The class itself does not only consist of listening to her talk on and on for 1 hour. Instead, she divide it between lectures, interactive exercises, videos, mini case analysis, and discussions. You will never get bored.

We also get to do a lot of personality tests and its always fun to know more about yourself, especially with Lucia to explain what each of the personality means and its strengths and weaknesses etc.

Always finishes class 10-15 minutes early after taking attendance by IPRS. She will stay in class for students who want to ask her questions. Very helpful and genuinely wants her students to understand and have fun learning.

Best professor in UST!
sections.grading:
Examination I MC (60 MCQ) 20%
Examination II Essay (6 LQ) 30%
Team project 30%
Class participation 14% (4% + 3% + 7%)
Research participation 6%

You are only allowed to bring in a 4x6" reference card for the midterm exam, and an A4 cheat sheet for final exam.

Class participation is attendance for 2 in-class activities (each 2%), presentation day attendance (3 days, each 1%) and regular class attendance (use IPRS to answer 5 questions based on the previous lecture in each class, count best 10 out of 14). You can skip up to 4 regular classes and still get full class participation. sections.content:
This course is about Organizational Behavior. From my perspective, OB is somehow like common sense, but professor says it isn't. There are three levels of outcomes in OB, and they are individual level, group level and organizational level. This course mainly discusses about the individual level and group level. (Though contents might vary from sessions to sessions)

Contents:
1. First, it talks about What is OB?
2. In individual level of OB, it talks about Personality and Values, Emotion, Perception and Decision Making, and Motivation.
3. In group level of OB, it talks about Groups and Teams, Communication, and Leadership.
4. At last, it talks about Managing Globally.
sections.teaching:
Carmen is always well prepared with the lecture. All the slides are well designed by herself, with interesting games, pictures, stories and videos. She will provide all the printed material for all students before the class, because she believe taking notes on the paper is much better than taking notes on the laptop. BTW, she will remember all your faces, do raise hands during the lectures!
However, she speaks a little bit fast, and there are some blanks on the lecture notes. You need to pay full attention in the lecture to take down what she says. (The exams will test the discussion in the lecture, you had better to take those notes down!)
sections.grading:
My midterm is mean, final is mean + 1SD.
Project gains the highest score. (mean + 1SD)
The overall grade is A-. I am pretty satisfied.

The grading is assigned by the following.
1. Class Participation (14%)
I tick attendance in the box, because there will be iPRS every lecture. But I remember she says 75% participation is enough for her. Do raise questions and answer questions, she will remember all your faces!
2. Mid-Term (60 Multiple Choices) (20%)
Closed book, do look through all your lecture notes and understand the concepts.
3. Final (6 Questions) (30%)
One two-side A4 cheat sheet.
4. Team Project (Presentation + Written Report) (30%)
Group in 5. Choose your interested movie and analyze the OB inside the movie.
5. Research Participation (6%)
Attend three 1-hour research (2% each), you will receive e-mail notification, register early!
sections.workload:
No homework.
3 research participation, 1 project, 1 midterm, 1 final.
I think this course is all about understanding and remembering! There are some workload during the project and right before the exams!

sections.content: The content for this course is extremely easy and straightforward. Insanely easy for anyone to understand. Definitely some of the easiest course material I have had in university, however it is anything but interesting. The course gets boring extremely quickly because everything we're learning seems to be the same thing as applying logic.
sections.teaching: Riki is quite a nice guy. He loves talking (especially about himself and his research) and is generally quite chill. However, his lectures aren't that interesting or stimulating, especially since he is quite monotone in his speech. Also, he has a rather bad habit of forgetting to provide us with details for assignments. For example, he asked us to write an "introduction card" for our group project but gave no explanation as to what that's supposed to mean. Only on the due date when it was brought to his attention that he didn't explain the assignment did he clarify what he looked for (the due date was postponed). There were many similar instances. He often isn't clear.
sections.grading: Wonderful. My midterm was roughly 1 sd above mean. I have no clue what my final exam score was but I assume I did extremely well. I also assume did well for the major project. There was no transparency on grading before the final grade came out. Final score A+.
sections.workload: Light. Other than the term project, there is no work outside of class. There is one midterm and one final, as well as one project that includes an essay and a presentation. But extremely easy to handle.

sections.content: Organizational Behavior is about personality, leadership, and others. Some of the content is similar to a psychological course but in a more business way

sections.grading: Grading is good. Even my team only get half of the participation point and a fair performance in presentation, I still get good grade.
sections.workload: Although there is a project about analyzing a movie, it is interesting and quite fun.

sections.content: Interesting content where many relevant concepts are studied. It was my first time taking a MGMT course and after doing so, it made me want to choose it as a major.
sections.teaching: Profesor Farh is proactive and encourages in-class participation. He will also give you help when you need it.
sections.grading: Good grades if you hand in your work in time and properly. The exams are not difficult if you study for it.
sections.workload: The workload is quite heavy but it can be divided amongst your friends because a large part of the grade is based on the group project.

sections.content: The content itself was really interesting, and it also seemed very practical and applicable to real life. A lot of it is based on concepts from psychology and sociology, so it helps if you have a background in those subjects (you might be a little bit more familiar with the terms etc).
sections.teaching: Professor Farh is a really engaging professor who tries his very best to make sure his students understand the content and are coping well with the workload. He is always open to answering questions, and is very helpful. I approached him a few times with regards to the group project, and he was very helpful and even sent me some research journals related to the topic of our research paper. He is really kind and approachable, and is definitely one of the friendliest professors I've had.
sections.grading: The grading was pretty decent for the course. There is one midterm, a group project (research paper), in-class exercises, attendance, and a final exam which make up your final grade for the course. In the midterm, I got 1 SD above mean, however I don't know the marks for my final exam or report as they were not released (however, I was very satisfied with my performance on both and think I did well). In-class attendance is taken through the PRS system, and it helps to go to lecture as participation makes up around 14% of your grade. In the end, I got an A+ for this course.
sections.workload: The workload was alright, as there are assigned readings before each class. Although it is not required, I recommend you do the readings as they help you to keep up with the material on the class. Also, the final exam had some questions on content which was in the assigned readings but wasn't covered explicitly in class, so I advise you to complete the readings. The majority of the workload, however, comes from the group project where you have to write a research paper on a OB topic (you are given 4 general areas, and have to choose one). If you have group mates that don't do much, good luck, because you'll need it. I highly recommend that you DON'T leave the paper until the last minute, because it takes a lot of time and effort to produce a good and thorough paper. There is also a presentation to complete based on your research paper, however it's not as tough and the professor is quite lenient with the presentation (just make it interesting and engaging and Professor Farh will like it).

sections.content: Alot of psychology and quite interesting material, but you still need to learn it book style and know all the correct terms. It's fun material in itself but learning all the proper terms can be draining.
sections.teaching: Larry tries to keep things interesting with in class activities and giving out papers for participation, so people are really active. He is a very nice professor who genuinely tries to help. He coached me through my entire group paper when my group decided to vanish into thin air.
sections.grading: Very fair grading, plus extra marks if you participate and come to office hours. I participated alot and went to alot of office hours and got an A+, even though my assignment and test marks were in the A- range. Put in the effort and let it show and you can get an amazing mark.
sections.workload: Not too bad! There is reading before class which are not mandatory but i suggest you do. There are also in class PRS which really only measure attendance.

Thus there was not really chance to learn about management which is quite awkward knowing that this course is about management anyways.
sections.teaching: The professor was really good in terms of his teaching skills. He prepares lots of examples to stimulate your understanding about a concept covered in his lecture. He also prepares lots of exercises in classes. If you are a kind of student who dislikes practice exercise to be graded, this is not a course for you. However, I really enjoyed most exercises in the course and the professor was really a pleasure to have.
sections.grading: I did not really have chance to review my exams (e.g. which questions I got right and wrong); For midterm I got 0.5 STDEV above and for final I did not get the standard deviation and the score. For rest of assignments the professor commented on our performance but once again, I did not have a chance to look and compare my score to others. However, the grading itself overall is okay.

sections.teaching: Lucia was a very bouncy professor. She had a lot of energy and every lesson was entertaining. And for that sole reason, I actually enjoyed the class.
sections.grading: Scoring high is relatively easy if you study - I found that a lot of students perceived OB as a bs class and for that did not study for their exams. There were small details like what personality type is it when a person is sociable - and you have to refer to Holland's Personality Types for that (she barely touched on it during the lecture). I scored 2 sds above the mean for the midterm and for the final and was able to attain an A+ even though our group presentation was meh.

sections.content:
There are three levels in organization but in this course we will only study the first two parts - individual and group.
　
1) Personalities and Values
2) Attitudes and Job Satisfaction
3) Emotions and Moods
4) Motivations
5) Perception and Individual Decision Making
6) Team Dynamics
7) Communications
8) Conflicts and Negotiation

Actually there is "leadership and power" in our syllabus but we didn't manage to cover it.

In general the class is fun and the concepts are interesting. Get a textbook because lecture notes are insufficient for exam preparation.
sections.teaching: Prof. Chao is really enthusiastic and willing to listen to students' feedback. The vibe is quite strange for my class, classmates rarely talk or respond to the questions, probably due to morning schedule and everyone is sleepy lol.
sections.grading:
Examination I                - 20% (80 points)
Examination II               - 30% (120 points)
Group project               - 30% (120 points)
Class participation        - 14% (56 points)
Research participation  - 6% (24 points)

Examination I (midterms) is MCQ and it's not that hard if you study the concepts in the textbook thoroughly. Examination II (final) is essay writing and one cheat sheet is allowed for the exam. Final is non-cumulative covering the second part of course. Group project is a disaster if you have free riders in the group, it is divided into two parts, written report (15%) and presentation (15%). Participation is basically attendance and some group activities.

The final grade is rather disappointing tho. I scored 1.2SD higher in midterms and participated in class actively but end up only B+. I emailed Prof. Chao and the TA regarding the grade and the reason is that I did badly for my final short essays even though my marks for midterm, long essay and participation are above average. So probably everyone is good in the examination and the curve is steep :O (Guess this is the norm of business school?)
sections.workload: Workload is actually okay. It really depends on your group members as some groups with good chemistry can work out but as in my case, I did most parts of my group project (contributing ideas, structures, write-up etc) report so it almost killed me especially there were few other projects on-going in the semester lol.

sections.teaching:
Lucia is a really good professor with advanced presentation skills, she is able to present all the materials clearly and interestingly, and engage all of the students in the lecture. She remembers all of her students' name and she can name you when you ask/answer questions. She cares about students a lot and will ask us questions like how do you feel or how can I make you feel better... She is also very kind and willing to answer your questions, both in the lecture and after the lecture.

In the lecture, she encourages us to speak and participate in class, so we had many inclass group discussion. It is really a relaxing but informative class.

If you can, choose her lecture, I think this will be a good choice for most students.
sections.grading:
She has high demand in the presentation (groups mostly getting only average marks, you can only score a 4 or above in a 5-point scale if you perform really well). BUT, in terms of final grading, she is very lenient.

The final exam is crucial to get a good grade, as the marks of us for previous exams and assignments are packed tightly.

Heard that people who score below mean for 2SD in mid-term with fair performance in project and final can still secure a B-.

The mean of her lectures may be B or even higher.

sections.content:
I came in to this class not expecting to like it, but it turns out I was wrong.

Course content is very realistic, and the professor will do his utmost best to prove that to you, using experiments, cases, etc.

The course is borderline intro to psych, and goes through aspects such as behavior, personality, value systems, group and individual decision making, team processes, leadership, communication, etc.
sections.teaching:
Prof. Raja has been one of my best professors thus far in HKUST. He puts in real effort into all of his lectures, meticulously planning how to ensure maximum knowledge retention.

Structure of most classes is quite similar, in the sense that he begins with a PowerPoint and some theories, then goes on to show you a couple videos about the same / a case / group exercise, and then finishes it off with takeaways. His teaching is very structured.
sections.grading:
Since it's a fairly easy course, and he allows cheatsheets for the exams, the course means are generally quite high.

Participation in Class 14%: You get one card for every time you answer a question in class, and 10 cards usually means you will get perfect score.

Research Participation 6%: Department policy, attend 3 studies, and receive the points.

Midterm 15%: MCQ based midterm, based solely of what he has gone through in class [if he didn't cover it in class, you don't have to study it]. Midterm has a high mean, it was around 82% for my class.

Assignment 40% (20% presentation, 16% report, 4% progress report: Need to select a movie and analyze the OB theories within it, and present findings. Progress report is a simple 1 page report that you submit a month into the course, then you do a presentation to the whole class, and also prepare a comprehensive report of your findings.
*Innovativeness and creativity will be rewarded in your presentations.
**Class vote at the end of each day of presentation ,and winner receives bonus marks.

Final Exam 25%: Non cumulative exam, semi MCQ, semi essay based. Similar comment to the Midterm.

- About the exams, it is vital that you attend classes, and take part actively in the cases and experiments. Questions about these come up very regularly in his exams, as he is an avid believer in the takeaways/conclusions, as opposed to the theories themselves.
sections.workload:
Workload is not heavy at all if you manage your time and your group effectively.

Straightforward course, and if you do what he asks, you should do well.

sections.grading:
Disclaimer: I got an A, so treat this part with a pinch of salt.

Exams: mostly MCQs, but there are essay questions in the final exam. Be careful: the seemingly unimportant in-class experiment/exercise that you missed could end up as an essay question...

Project: there were 4 options, all broad topics. After choosing one of them, your group should come up with a reasonably specific question. And then work on it. Finally give a presentation and report about the topic. Tip: remember to consult your prof - 1. You can let him recognize you, 2. You can get to know his preference. Just ask him indirectly - he's nice enough to tell you a lot more than you need ;)
I didn't meet anyone that free-rides or doesn't cooperate well - but if you do, make sure you keep your evidence (in case you end up reporting...)

Participation:
1. Be present (and sign up) for in-class experiments.
2. Make hin recognize you by always bringing your name tag to class, and answering enough questions to earn you 2 participation cards every class*. Otherwise, you can ask him questions or go to online discussions. Better still, initiate discussions there :)
* that's what I did, but you don't have to - he will remind you of how the parti scores are calculated, and you'll realise that it's helpful but not necessary.
